status: all focused, local, Worker, conformance, reference, release and public-R2 gates passed
problem: Generic SharedMemoryCache inserts charged payloads but omitted map-record and retained-key storage. Zero-byte payloads could accumulate unbounded entries, and decoded-cache keys remained retained after their construction scratch was released.
contract: Account for record, directory slot and retained UTF-16 key in both configured cache capacity and its shared allocation pool.
Keep metadata ownership separate from payload ownership: eviction releases keys and records while independent readers continue to pin payloads.
Admit payload and metadata before ordinary allocation factories; release both on failure.
Owned insertion directly retains the payload and separately admits cache metadata; insertion remains optional.
Move metadata accounting out of the planning-cache wrapper and object-store payload forecasts into the generic cache.
Clean up reentrant same-key inserts before publishing an outer factory result.
Validate finite safe cache capacities and finite non-negative TTL centrally; zero capacity disables all retention.
Reject entries that cannot displace protected cache priorities before their metadata admission can reclaim those entries.
Read-ahead forecasts include payload, entry metadata, cache capacity, query extent and unreserved shared-pool headroom.

validation.negativeControl: All 12 generic-cache regressions fail against 47606b7 behavior. Only the candidate metadata-size formula was exposed to baseline tests; insertion/retention behavior was unchanged.

initialFullSuite.note: Intermediate diagnostic run; all reported integration failures were resolved before publication gates.

publicR2.fourWindowFixture: 4,096 payload bytes plus entry metadata: legacy capacity 7,770 bytes, owned capacity 7,818 bytes; original 64/128 MiB pool caps unchanged. Ordinary-query 512 KiB headroom is unchanged.

remaining: Transient key construction and prefix workspace admission remain separate from retained-key accounting.
Remaining parser/converter/codec and execution allocation matrix items and total runtime memory caps remain open.

measurements.scope: No cloud-throughput or total-runtime-memory guarantee. Cache insertion is more fully accounted, not a speedup. Equal cache caps retain fewer entries when metadata is significant.
